question.leadin: Albert Einstein turned down the presidency of this country.
question.text: Identify this country that declared independence in 1948 following the end of British rule in Mandatory Palestine. It is the only officially Jewish country in the world.
question.clue: This nation's city of Beersheba is known as the "capital of the Negev".

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about prominent terrorist groups.
swap.text: This group, led by Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi, was responsible for the attacks in November 2015 on Paris that killed 130 people.
swap.clue: Brett McGurk is the American special envoy to a coalition against this group.

question.text: This Islamic political organization was suppressed during Mubarak's time in office, but formed the Freedom and Justice Party to contest elections after Mubarak's resignation.
question.answerHtml: Muslim Brotherhood (accept The Society of the Muslim Brothers)
question.clue: Its first meeting place was created in Ismailia by its founder Hassan al-Bannah ("HAH-sen al-buh-NAH").

swap.leadin: In the weeks after this man was overthrown in a July 3, 2013 military coup, he was said to be in a "safe place" but had not made a public appearance.
swap.text: Name this former President of the Muslim Brotherhood's political party, the Freedom and Justice Party, who was elected President of his nation in 2012, shortly after the downfall of Hosni Mubarak.
swap.clue: This leader defeated the Salafist Nour party to win his first election.

question.leadin: This empire was defeated at the Battle of Tours.
question.text: Name this empire founded by Muawiyah which defeated its predecessor at the Battle of Siffin. An offshoot of this empire after its fall would later form the Emirate of Cordoba under Abd al-Rahman I.
question.clue: Their main branch, which got a reputation for drunkenness, fell after Marwan II lost the Battle of Zab.

swap.leadin: The Mamluks constructed a series of warehouses called khans along the road from this city to the "breadbasket" region of Hauran.
swap.text: Name this city which was the seat of the Umayyad Caliphate. This city names a rare style of flowing steel.
swap.clue: Saladin left Egypt to establish an Ayyubid sultanate at this city, which would be the site of his death.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Turkish migration from Central Asia.
question.text: This second sultan of the Seljuqs fought a war against the Fatimids in Syria. He defeated the Byzantine army at the Battle of Manzikert, where he captured the Byzantine emperor Romanos IV.
question.answerHtml: Alp Arslan [accept Muhammad bin Dawud Chaghri , prompt on Heroic Lion ]
question.clue: According to Edward Gibbon, this man died when he waved his bodyguards away and tried to shoot an assassin with his own bow.

swap.text: At first, some suspected the explosion to have been the result of a terrorist attack by this Shiite terrorist group. This terrorist group is led by Hassan Nasrallah, and was heavily backed by Iranian commander Qassem Soleimani.
swap.clue: Led by Hassan Nasrallah, and given major funding by Iran, this group's 2006 kidnapping of Israeli soldiers sparked a brief war between Israel and the country which it controls large parts of.

question.text: The Egyptian brigade was named after the Battle of Ayn Jalut, in which Sultan Qutuz, who was this type of slave soldier, defeated the invading Mongols. Thereafter, these slave-sultans ruled Egypt until 1516.
question.clue: They followed the furusiyya code, which includes cavalry tactics and horsemanship.

swap.leadin: The British government formally endorsed this idea in the Balfour Declaration.
swap.text: Name this doctrine holding that the Jewish people should have their own homeland.
swap.clue: That letter supporting this cause was written by Foreign Secretary Arthur Balfour.

question.text: On his way to the Holy Land, Richard conquered Cyprus, which he traded to the Knights Templar, who eventually ceded it to this leader of the Lusignan dynasty. This guy had previously been king of the Jerusalem crusader state.

swap.leadin: Lisa Anderson claimed that a "Facebook Revolution" as part of this larger series of events was a modern arm of existing nationalist networks.
swap.text: Social media helped spread and document what early 2010s wave of unrest that toppled leaders like Ali Abdullah Saleh and Zine El Abidine Ben Ali?
swap.clue: One government destroyed the Pearl Roundabout, a gathering place for protests during this period.

question.leadin: During a 1974 military operation, this capital city's Ledra Palace Hotel was assaulted by paratroopers who had earlier captured the highway supplying it from Kyrenia.
question.text: Name this city, where a hospital containing British-held prisoners was stormed by EOKA ("ee-OH-kuh") under Georgios Grivas. The Occupy Buffer Zone movement demonstrated against the Green Line in this city's Eleftheria ("eh-leff-THEH-ree-uh") Square.
question.clue: The Cypriot "Occupy Buffer Zone" movement has made a permanent encampment at the Ledra Street crossing point in this divided capital of Cyprus.

swap.text: Mevlevlis considering whirling a form of this type of "remembrance" by which one gets closer to God and is able to feel God's presence.
swap.clue: One of the main ways that Sufis demonstrate their devotion is through this rhythmic repetition of the name of Allah.

question.text: After Gemayel's assassination, the IDF gave Phalangist militias access to a refugee camp and a Shia neighborhood in Beirut, resulting in this massacre that forced Ariel Sharon ("sha-ROHN") to resign as defense minister.
question.clue: Elie Hobeika's forces were able to carry on slaughtering people through the night thanks to flares fired from a third party, which led the Kahan Commission to declare the sitting Defense Minister "personally responsible."

swap.leadin: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muljam, a member of this sect of Islam, plotted to kill Mu'awiyya, 'Amr ibn-al-'As, and another leader all on the same day with a poisoned saber. He only succeeded once.
swap.text: The aforementioned dude was a member of this sect, whose name comes from their withdrawal from mainstream Islam after a certain dude hero-worshipped in Iran agreed to arbitration with Mu'awiyya.
swap.clue: Once selected as Caliph, Ali faced several revolts during the First Fitna, including by this breakaway sect which Ali defeated at the Battle of Nahrawan.

question.leadin: This man provided refuge for the German diplomat Fritz Grobba, and was persuaded by his adviser Harry St. John Philby to award concessions to American companies.
question.text: Name this man who conquered Najd and the Hejaz, and defeated the Ikhwan, before consolidating his holdings and founding a kingdom in 1932.
question.answerHtml: Ibn Saud [or Abdulaziz ibn Abdul Rahman ibn Faisal ibn Turki ibn Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Saud; or Abdulaziz]
question.clue: This man's successor is the namesake of the third largest city in Pakistan.

swap.text: The first Umayyad, Abu Sufyan, was a member of this tribe, which controlled Mecca during the time of Muhammad. Divisions of this tribe included the Banu Hashim.
swap.answerHtml: Quraysh [or Kuraish or Koreish or Quresh or Qurrish or Qurish or Qirsh or Qureshi or Coreish]
swap.clue: Muhammad's Hashemites were one of 10 clans in this ruling tribe of Mecca. The Umayyads and Rashiduns traced their lineage to other clans in this group of peoples.

question.text: This golden-voiced friend of Muhammad was born into slavery as the son of Ethiopian princess captured during the Abyssinian attempt to destroy the Kaaba during the Year of the Elephant. He was later freed and became the first muezzin.
question.answerHtml: Bilal ibn Rabah [or Bilal al-Habashi; or Bilal ibn Riyah; prompt on “ibn Rabah” or “al- Habashi” or “ibn Riyah”]

swap.leadin: Answer the following about some Middle Eastern events that happened in 1990.
swap.text: In 1990, Saddam Hussein sent his army on this campaign, which successfully brought rich oil fields under Hussein's control. It was the major impetus for the Gulf War.
swap.answerHtml: the Iraqi invasion of Kuwait [in place of “invasion,” accept: obvious equivalents]
swap.clue: The aggressor in this event accused its neighbor of cross drilling into the Rumaila Oil Field.
